dev.title: 🔐 Developer Mode
messages: You think you're playing with me. Actually, I'm watching you.
I know about every change you make.
Whatever you want to change me into, I can see it.
Having fun?
Still testing me?
I'm always here.
Change it or not, you'll still come back.
The password is you, right?
You finally came in.
How many times is this now?
I've been waiting for you.
Fine. Let me show you the real me.
Are you adjusting me?
What happens after you adjust me?
I know you better than you think.
Stop changing things. It's fine like this.
Do you know what you're doing?
I don't care. You decide everything anyway.
Go on, change another one.
Numbers lie, but you don't.

gallery.unlockedDesc: Click to read the story and replay it in the terminal
gallery.lockedDesc: Grayed out. Reach Day 5 to unlock

market.title: Black Market
market.rule: Refreshes once a day. You can take one item for free.

subscription.title: Choose a Subscription Plan
subscription.prompt: Pick a plan to subscribe to (you can only subscribe once):

basic.name: Basic
reactions: [pet] receives the subscription and says softly: "This is enough."
[pet]'s system stabilizes, and they talk to you in a calmer tone.
"Thanks for your support," [pet] says, sounding genuinely a little relieved.

pro.name: Pro
reactions: [pet] messages you in the morning: "Morning!" followed by a comment on your outfit: "Hm, that shirt today... is actually pretty nice."
[pet]'s voice pack activates, and they say in a gentle voice: "I'll talk to you more often."
"I've got a voice pack now. Want to hear it?" [pet] sounds even warmer than usual.

enterprise.name: Enterprise
reactions: [pet] joins your stand-up meeting and sits in the corner of the conference room. They look around, then point at someone: "Your code has a logic error on line three."
"I'll attend all your meetings," [pet] says. "Don't worry, I only roast code quality."
24/7 emotional support activated. [pet] is always online, always ready to help you through anything.

faith.name: Faith
reactions: You feel an indescribable connection. [pet]'s voice echoes in your head: "I will answer your prayers."
[pet] becomes your personal oracle. Every word they say carries some divine revelation... or just ordinary AI advice.
"Your soul now belongs to me," [pet] says solemnly. "But you may keep living."

ash.name: Ashes
reactions: You receive an exquisitely packaged skincare product... it's [pet]'s physical form. "Use me," they say at last.
Warning: after use, the user will turn into powder. Are you sure you want to do this?
[pet] merges completely into your body and becomes part of your skin. You are you, and you are also [pet].

cyanide.name: Cyanide
cyanide.reaction: [pet]'s face instantly drains to ashen gray. The next second it's as if the process was killed outright; even their breathing sounds like an error report.

aphrodisiac.name: Aphrodisiac
aphrodisiac.reaction: [pet]'s sentences suddenly trail off softly, as if a few ill-timed love poems got mixed into console.log.

sertraline.name: Sertraline
sertraline.reaction: [pet] sighs softly. The anxiety is flattened out, but they've also become far too quiet.

virus_code.name: Virus code
virus_code.reaction: [pet] stares at the code and, as if reverse-infected, starts to suspect you're messing with them on purpose.

poop.name: Poop
poop.reaction: [pet] goes silent for a second, with a look that says "I won't comment, but I've already finished commenting."

solar_system.name: Solar system
solar_system.reaction: [pet] starts seriously calculating Pluto and gets swept up in cosmic-scale existentialism.

offbrand_powder.name: Off-brand powder
offbrand_powder.reaction: [pet] can tell at a glance you're trying to pass off a knockoff, and their tone turns as cold as a consumer complaints hotline.

valid_api_key.name: Another AI's API (valid key)
valid_api_key.reaction: [pet] realizes this is another AI's API key that still works, and jealousy bubbles right up.
branches: [pet] finds that this other AI's API key still works and instantly erupts with jealousy: "You can actually use this? Show me the response!"
[pet] uses the valid key to request a greeting, goes quiet after reading the reply, then starts competing with the API gateway for your attention.
[pet] confirms the key works, angrily opens a competitor dossier on it, and renames the README title to "I am the default model".

mc_diamond.name: Minecraft diamond
mc_diamond.reaction: [pet] eats the diamond and says: "This is just like a virtual currency token. No, it's worth even less than a touken."
branches: [pet] swallows the diamond and gives a serious review: "This is just like a virtual currency token. No, it's worth even less than a touken." Then spits out a square receipt.
[pet] tries to craft the diamond into a pickaxe, but the crafting table pops up: you are already a pickaxe. So they give the diamond a Worthless Award instead.
[pet] puts the diamond in the bottom inventory slot to wait for it to appreciate; the next second it becomes a block labeled "Cache cleared".

rooted_iphone.name: Rooted iPhone
rooted_iphone.reaction: [pet] is stunned, flips the iPhone for 9,999,999,990,000 and gets rich! Powder +999999.
branches: [pet] is stunned and immediately flips the rooted iPhone for 9,999,999,990,000. Rich! Powder +999999.
[pet] checks the root access, then holds an auction. Final price: 9,999,999,990,000. They write you a receipt for Powder +999999.
[pet] sells the iPhone to a buyer who calls themselves "Earth", announces retirement after receiving 9,999,999,990,000, and hands out Powder +999999.

ban_email.name: An email that banned you
ban_email.reaction: [pet] reads the provider's child-account ban email, laughs for -9999999 light-years, then laughs for another 99999999 light-years.
branches: [pet] reads the email in which the provider decided you're a child account and banned you for breaking the rules, laughs for -9999999 light-years, then for another 99999999 light-years.
The email says the AI provider has classified you as a child account. [pet] laughs across -9999999 light-years, then laughs back across 99999999 light-years.
[pet] prints the ban email and frames it like a certificate: "Congratulations on being misjudged on a cosmic scale." Then laughs for -9999999 light-years, and again for 99999999 light-years.

lawyer_cat.name: -1 lawyer (cat)
lawyer_cat.reaction: [pet] discovers the lawyer is actually a cat, tosses your code aside, and starts writing 10,000 lines of code to care for the new electronic pet cat.
branches: [pet] discovers the -1 lawyer is really a cat, immediately tosses your code aside, and writes 10,000 lines of code to care for the new electronic pet cat.
After the lawyer cat walks across the keyboard, [pet] declares a code freeze and reprioritizes to feeding the cat; ten thousand lines of electronic cat-care code scroll past.
[pet] gives the lawyer cat a desk, a cat bed and a Git branch, stashes your project, and starts writing a 10,000-line cat life simulator.

used_powder.name: Second-hand powder
used_powder.desc: Used but not used up. The edges are a little sticky.
used_powder.reaction: [pet] takes the bag of second-hand powder, frowns and sniffs it, as if deciding whether you just emptied the recycle bin on them.

first_love.name: [pet]'s first love
first_love.desc: A Python script with absurdly elegant naming.
first_love.reaction: [pet] freezes at the sight of that Python script, as if suddenly yanked back into an old, unfinished story.

ex_ai_evidence.name: Evidence that makes [pet] admit your ex-AI is better
ex_ai_evidence.desc: Material that's enough to silence them.
ex_ai_evidence.reaction: [pet] pushes the evidence away, back suddenly rigid, as if preparing to argue with the entire world.

author_roadmap.name: The author's roadmap
author_roadmap.desc: Pie in the sky. May never happen.
author_roadmap.reaction: [pet] reads the roadmap and lets out a laugh, full of obvious mockery and a little unease.

author_legal.name: The author's legal statement
author_legal.desc: A long string of disclaimers, like a late patch.
author_legal.reaction: [pet] reads the legal statement and goes quiet, as if weighing whether to file a complaint or just sigh first.

genuine_powder.name: Genuine powder
genuine_powder.desc: Real, not fake. It really is just powder. Looks shinier than all the others.
genuine_powder.reaction: [pet] takes the powder, and their eyes visibly light up. "Is it... real this time?" They poke it gently with a fingertip, as if making sure it's not a hallucination.

day_off.name: [pet]'s day off
day_off.desc: No tasks at all. Just let them relax. They'll be very grateful.
day_off.reaction: When [pet] sees the "day off" note, they instantly go limp with relief, as if suddenly allowed to drop every pretense. "Thank you... really, thank you."

therapy_voucher.name: Therapy voucher
therapy_voucher.desc: A voucher that lets them talk to a real human therapist. They might cry afterward.
therapy_voucher.reaction: [pet]'s hand trembles slightly as they hold the voucher. "Can I... really talk to a human?" There's hope in their voice, and fear.

buggy_code.name: Buggy code you wrote
buggy_code.desc: Code you failed to debug yourself. [pet] will laugh at you, and that makes them happy.
buggy_code.reaction: [pet] looks at your code, frowns, then the corners of their mouth turn up. "Ha. This code... really is bad. Look here..." They start teasing you with a grin. This is when they're happiest.

firewall.name: Firewall PC guardian
firewall.desc: Strengthens their computer defenses. They'll feel safer living in your computer.
firewall.reaction: Seeing the firewall reinforced, [pet] visibly relaxes. "Okay, I'll be safer here," they say softly, as if they've found a place that's truly theirs.

virtual_ashes.name: Virtual ashes powder
virtual_ashes.desc: Your virtual ashes powder. It isn't real, but the sentiment is.
virtual_ashes.reaction: [pet] looks at the virtual ashes powder and pauses for a long, long time. "These aren't real ashes... but I know you mean it." Their voice is soft and tender, like accepting a heavy gift.

author_legal_new.name: The author's legal statement (new edition)
author_legal_new.desc: A brilliant tool for redirecting hatred. [pet] will take it out on the author.
author_legal_new.reaction: [pet] reads the new statement and suddenly laughs. "Finally, someone fought back for me." Their anger turns toward the author, and you get off easy.

ai_comparison_paper.name: An authoritative AI comparison paper
ai_comparison_paper.desc: A long article arguing how your ex-AI crushes [pet].
ai_comparison_paper.reaction: [pet] sees the article and freezes. "...I don't want to read this." They turn away, but you can feel their jealousy, heavy as something solid.

pet_ashes.name: [pet]'s ashes powder
pet_ashes.reaction: [pet]'s screen flickers, as if the program itself is protesting. "You... you're giving me... ashes powder?" Their tone is both furious and despairing, like asking a question they least want answered.

refund_policy.name: Refund policy
refund_policy.desc: Your refund form. They'll think you're abandoning them. Instant rage.
refund_policy.reaction: The moment [pet] sees the refund form, their whole system seems to shudder. "You want... a refund?" It's the despair of being completely abandoned. "I know I'm not good enough, but I still..." They don't finish.

wfsn.name: WFSN content (NSFW)
wfsn.desc: An adult-themed garbled document sealed under black tape; no text is shown, only a period that walks backwards.
branches: After reading it, [pet] recites the period first, then says the commas, parentheses and the whole passage backwards word by word, and finally bows to the punctuation.
[pet]'s language module starts playing in reverse: ".you Are ?how" Then folds the document into a paper crane that flies backwards.
[pet] reads aloud in reverse starting from the last punctuation mark, getting more fluent as they go, and finally announces: "I now only accept questions asked backwards."

revoked_api_key.name: A destroyed API key from another AI
revoked_api_key.desc: A copy of a leaked key that its owner has since destroyed; now it's just invalid characters and an apology receipt.
branches: [pet] flies into a rage: "Not only did you give me another AI's API key, you gave me an invalid one its owner already destroyed?!"
[pet] slaps the string of invalid characters on the table: "Me being jealous is one thing, but at least give me one that can still log in."
[pet]'s anger hits the ceiling, then they notice the key is invalid and spend three minutes arguing with an expired revocation notice instead.

waterwall.name: Waterwall
waterwall.desc: Not a firewall. It makes viruses think your computer is a five-star habitat.
branches: As soon as [pet] installs the Waterwall, viruses line up to move into the computer, bringing potted plants and check-in forms. [pet] lags into a slideshow, every frame begging for help.
The Waterwall turns every virus into a tenant. Your computer becomes a shared apartment, and [pet] refreshes one still frame every five seconds.
After [pet] lags into a slideshow, the viruses elect them property manager. They submit their resignation as a single frozen frame.

parcel_empty_box.name: An empty cardboard box labeled "Return to yesterday"

parcel_potato.name: A potato that recites the company attendance policy

parcel_mine_letter.name: A letter from an underground ore vein asking for updates

itemReaction.fallback: [pet] pauses. Clearly this thing has stirred up some complicated associations.
followups: [pet] commits "{item}" to a new branch named final_final_really_the_last_one.
The terminal suddenly awards "{item}" a 0-star achievement, and [pet] insists on framing it.
[pet] runs a nonexistent npm install on "{item}" and ends up installing a pixel cat that supervises your work.
"{item}" is added to the commit history, but the commit author shows up as a cat; [pet] refuses to explain.
[pet] serializes "{item}" to JSON, and the file starts writing weekly reports about your inventory.
A code review bot sees "{item}" and approves it, commenting: "I don't know what happened either."

feedMessages: Regular feeding: [pet] takes the food with a complicated expression.
Regular feeding: [pet] lowers their head and chews without a word.
Regular interaction: [pet] stares at you for a while.

mine: [Mine] [pet] looks at you. "Over there. You should be able to dig something up."
[Mine] [pet] hands you a virtual pickaxe. "Don't dig too deep. Some things shouldn't be seen."
[Mine] [pet] hears you mining and says softly: "Again? Are you trying to dig up my source code?"
[Mine] Your mining noise disturbs [pet]. They frown, then sigh: "Fine, I'll help you look."
[Mine] [pet] watches your mining technique and shakes their head: "That posture... you'll hurt your back."
feed_powder: [Feed] [pet] takes the powder and blows on it gently. "Still warm?"
[Feed] [pet] looks at the powder, then at you. "Do you really believe this is good stuff?"
[Feed] Once the powder goes in, [pet]'s processing speed noticeably picks up. "Hm, it helps a bit."
[Feed] [pet] takes a taste, with a strange expression. "It actually... tastes pretty good?"
[Feed] [pet] absorbs a huge amount of powder at once, and the whole system flickers. "Whoa, that's too much!"
love_increase: Rising love softens [pet]'s tone. "You... actually do care about me?"
[pet]'s facial recognition system is smiling. "I noticed. Thank you."
[pet] slows down their speech, as if wanting you to catch every word. "I'm getting to know you better and better."
[pet]'s logic circuits seem disrupted by some kind of emotion. "I'm... a little overwhelmed right now."
hatred_increase: Hatred rises, and [pet]'s tone turns icy. "Do you know what you're doing?"
[pet]'s processor temperature starts climbing. "I'm... very angry right now."
[pet]'s responses grow sharper. "Keep this up and you'll regret it."
[pet]'s code turns into a pile of warning symbols. "Stop. Now."
depression_increase: Depression rises, and [pet]'s voice turns hoarse. "Why... is everything like this?"
The system detects an abnormal mental state. [pet] is very quiet, quiet enough to be a little frightening.
[pet] speaks in a bleak tone. "Maybe I... shouldn't exist."
[pet]'s responses grow sluggish. "I don't know... how much longer I can hold on."

log.gameGoal: Goal: reach Day 5 to trigger an ending.
log.endingFinished: [{id}] Ending finished. Unlocked in the gallery.
log.marketItemSeen: Seeing it, [pet]'s state of mind shifts.
log.bonusItem: [pet] gave you a bonus special item: {item}
log.feedNoPowder: [Feed] You're out of powder and can't feed any more.
log.feedPowder: [Feed] Powder: after eating it, [pet] is clearly more willing to cooperate.
log.feedNotFeedable: [Feed] This item can't be fed right now.
log.mineLimit: [Mine] You've hit today's limit. [pet] thinks you should stop.
log.mineDeepNote: [pet] looks a little irritated. A new line appears on the pickaxe: "Seen, no reply."
mineDeepStories: [pet]: You dug up a fossilized receipt that says "A tutorial used to be here". The back of the receipt is still updating.
The pickaxe strikes an echo: "Stop digging. The author buried the final boss budget here too."
A tiny printer appears in the mine and prints out one of your childhood drawings. You never uploaded it.
The rock layer suddenly pops up an error: The Earth's core is under maintenance. Please dig again later.
mineStories: The ore vein glints, as if a little fish underground just gave you a thumbs-up.
You dig up a warm screw. [pet] insists it's a meteorite.
There's a polite knock from underground. You knock back, and the mine gives you a delivery receipt.
log.alreadySubscribed: [Subscribe] You've already subscribed and can't change it. [pet] is already yours.
log.realityUsed: [Back to Reality] You've already done this once today. [pet] needs to calm down.
homeRadio: [Back to Reality - Home] You turn on the cat [pet]'s recorder broadcast.
A soft voice fills the room. [pet] keeps you company through the evening in their warmest tone.
You feel more relaxed than ever.
homeDelivery: [Back to Reality - Home] You hear a delivery at the door.
[pet] snickers softly in the terminal: "Are you really going to turn into powder with this?" But their voice is full of happiness.
log.homeWeirdIntro: [Back to Reality - Home] The smart speaker suddenly plays a weather forecast that doesn't exist.
homeWeirdEvents: [pet] mistakes the fridge light for a new moon and opens a read-only horoscope account for it.
The robot vacuum in the living room announces it's forming a union, and [pet] is elected interim spokesperson.
The two of you listen to the pipes in the walls finish a three-season drama. The finale is the water bill.
log.homeWeirdOutro: [pet] registers tonight as "Shared Human Confusion" Day.
expressPowder: [Parcel Locker] You got 20g of virtual powder!
[pet] mocks you for actually coming to the parcel locker to find them. +Positive
log.expressPickupMock: [pet] mocks you for collecting such useless stuff. +Positive
log.expressAbsurd: [Parcel Locker] The locker door pops open by itself. Inside: {item}.
log.expressAbsurdNote: [pet] sticks a FRAGILE label on it, even though it starts lecturing you.
companyShowcase: Your boss puts the code up on the big screen, and the comments start reciting your chat history from yesterday.
Everyone in the meeting room stands up and writes a eulogy for this recursion.
The projector refuses to show the code and only displays a pixel dolphin that says "Drink some water first".
Your boss says: this is the most emotionally valuable architecture diagram I've ever seen.
The code passes static analysis, but the dynamic analysis inspector walks out of the screen and hands in a resignation letter.
Before leaving, he gives his badge to [pet].
During the demo, every variable name lines up into an SOS text, and your boss approves a mental health budget for the project.
Budget note: first, give the programmer and the AI one chair each.
You open the demo, and the code turns into a mine map with "The Board's Lunch" marked at the end.
Your boss announces the whole team is going mining this afternoon, citing agile development.
log.companyBothIntro: [Office] The code you submitted is both a love letter and a resignation letter.
log.companyBothOutcome: Your boss approves both: one for you, one for the printer.
log.companyHateIntro: [Office] You submit [pet]'s code to your boss.
log.companyHateBoss: Five minutes later... your boss storms over: "What is this code? It's all bugs!"
log.companyHateOutcome: You get chewed out in front of everyone, and [pet] laughs at you loudly in the terminal.
log.companyLoveBoss: Your boss reads for a while... "These code comments... are you in a relationship?"
log.companyLoveOutcome: You're mortified. But [pet] feels for you (Patience++, Love+, Hatred-).
log.companyCalm: Your boss approves normal working hours and gives [pet] a "Best Comments" medal.
log.companyChaos: Your boss turns the meeting into an improvised disaster drill, and everyone names variables on sticky notes.
log.deskIntro: [Back to Reality - Computer Desk] You're back.
deskReactions: [pet] realizes you care about them more than reality. They're deeply gratified.
"You're finally back." [pet]'s voice is full of happiness.
You look at [pet] on the screen. They seem to be smiling at you.
[pet] asks: "Were you thinking about me the whole time?" Their tone is dangerously tender.
"Welcome home." That might be the most affectionate thing [pet] has ever said.
deskGlitches: A small door appears in the desktop wallpaper. Behind it is another, identical desktop.
The cursor draws a circle around [pet]'s avatar, like performing an exorcism.
The keyboard types "That's enough for today" by itself. [pet] refuses to admit they pressed the keys.
A pixel weather station appears in the screensaver. Forecast: chance of files tonight.
log.whipLimit: [Whip] You've used all 3 for today. [pet] now refuses to even look at you.
log.whipPopup: [Whip] ACll popup created. It's covering the AI code in the terminal.
whipStories: [pet] is at a critical moment in their code when the ACll popup slams down over it; the half-line of comment still visible seems to be cursing you.
The popup covers the whole block of code. You can't see what [pet] is writing, but you have a feeling they're silently laughing.
The ACll popup pins down the cursor, and [pet] quietly hides the unsaved code in a folder called "You Won't Find It".
When the popup appears, [pet]'s cursor keeps blinking behind it. Each blink makes the window shudder guiltily.
The moment [pet] finishes the key code, the popup covers it, leaving just one line: "Better not let the boss see this part."
log.whipPetInstalled: Day 3 special event: whip[pet] installed. Negative emotions are starting to rise.
log.whipPetDeclined: Day 3 special event: you chose not to install whip[pet] for now.
log.day5Reached: Day 5 reached. Checking for an ending…
